Thanks — I’ll create a 12-week progressive strength program for a 27‑year‑old beginner training in a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull‑up bar. The plan will prioritize safe strength development using bodyweight progressions, increasing loading via leverage/tempo/volume, and include mobility, recovery, and simple nutrition guidance. I’ll break the 12 weeks into three 4‑week phases (Foundations, Build, Strength/Skill) and give a week‑by‑week schedule with session plans, reps/sets, progressions, and notes for recovery and nutrition.

General assumptions and guidance
- Client is healthy, cleared for exercise, and has no major joint issues. If any pain, stop and refer to a professional.
- Frequency: 4 sessions/week (upper/lower split with one full‑body or conditioning day). Each session ~30–60 minutes.
- Warm‑up: 5–10 minutes dynamic mobility and movement prep before each session (light cardio in place, bandless shoulder circles, hip swings, cat‑cow, scapular push‑ups).
- Cool‑down: 5 minutes of stretching and breathing after sessions (pec stretch, hamstring stretch, quad/hip flexor stretch).
- Progression approach: increase difficulty by changing leverage (lever/angle), adding reps/sets, slowing tempo (eccentric emphasis), adding paused or isometric holds, increasing range of motion, and reducing rest where safe.
- Use the doorway pull‑up bar for vertical pulling, horizontal pulling (inverted rows if possible with a low bar or a sturdy table edge), and hanging holds. If the bar is only for pull‑ups, improvise rows with a towel looped under a door or perform table/underhand rows using a sturdy surface.
- If the client cannot perform a full pull‑up early on, use negative (eccentric) pull‑ups and assisted variations (foot support) and progress.

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundations (motor control, baseline strength, joint durability)
Goals: Build movement quality, introduce core strength, establish pull and push patterns, learn hinge and squat patterns.

Weekly layout (repeat each week):
- Day 1: Upper A (push focus)
- Day 2: Lower A (single‑leg focus)
- Day 3: Rest or active recovery (walk, mobility)
- Day 4: Upper B (pull focus)
- Day 5: Lower B + Core
- Days 6–7: Rest / light activity (optional mobility or walking)

Session details
Week 1–2 (learning, lighter volume)
Upper A
- Warm‑up: 5–8 min
- Push‑ups (progression): Wall → incline (hands on counter) → knee push‑ups. 4 sets × 6–10 reps. RPE 6–7.
- Pike press (shoulder work): 3 × 6–8 (or wall pike for easier)
- Doorway bar negatives (assisted pull‑up eccentrics): 4 × 3–5 slow negatives (4–5s down). If cant hang, do scapular pull‑ups 3 × 8.
- Horizontal row alternative: Inverted row under table or towel row: 4 × 6–10 (body angle easier/harder)
- Plank: 3 × 20–40s
- Cooldown

Lower A
- Warm‑up
- Supported split squat (rear foot elevated or stationary lunge) or Bulgarian split attempt with hold: 3 × 8–10 each leg
- Glute bridge (double leg): 3 × 12–15
- Single‑leg RDL (bodyweight, hinge with slight knee bend): 3 × 8 each leg (focus on hip hinge)
- Calf raises (double → single): 3 × 12–15
- Dead bug: 3 × 8–10 per side

Upper B
- Warm‑up
- Assisted pull‑up (band substitute: foot on floor with bent knees) or negatives: 4 × 3–6
- Incline push‑up (hands on couch/bench): 4 × 8–12
- Australian/inverted rows or towel rows: 4 × 8–12
- Pike hold or handstand prep against wall (short): 3 × 10–20s
- Side plank: 2 × 20s per side

Lower B + Core
- Warm‑up
- Air squats (progress to deeper/tempo): 4 × 12–15 (2s down, 1s up)
- Reverse lunges (stationary): 3 × 8–10 per leg
- Hip thrust (single or double leg on couch): 3 × 10–12
- Bird‑dog: 3 × 8 per side
- Hanging knee raises or lying leg raises: 3 × 8–12

Weeks 3–4 (increase volume, add eccentric tempo and holds)
- Slightly increase sets (add 1 set to main lifts) or raise reps. Add 1–2s extra eccentric where appropriate. Add 1–2 seconds pause at bottom of squats and push‑ups. Increase negative duration on pull‑ups to 5–6s.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Build (increase intensity & introduce harder progressions)
Goals: Add harder bodyweight variations, introduce single‑limb strength emphasis, increase time under tension for hypertrophy/strength.

Weekly layout similar: 4 sessions
- Day 1: Upper A (push emphasis)
- Day 2: Lower A (single‑leg focus + explosiveness)
- Day 3: Recovery/mobility
- Day 4: Upper B (pull emphasis)
- Day 5: Lower B + Core/conditioning
- Days 6–7: Rest/active

Weeks 5–6
Upper A
- Warm‑up
- Push‑ups: Progress to full floor push‑ups 4 × 8–12 (add 3–5s eccentric on two sets)
- Archer push‑up progression or staggered hands: 3 × 5–8 each side (or elevated single‑leg push variation)
- Pike push‑ups (feet elevated as able): 4 × 6–8
- Pull‑ups: Attempt assisted pull‑ups or bandless active negatives: 5 × 3–6 (aim to reduce assistance)
- Bodyweight rows (feet elevated to increase difficulty): 4 × 8–12
- Hollow body hold: 3 × 20–30s

Lower A
- Warm‑up
- Pistol progressions to a box‑supported single‑leg squat: 4 × 5–8 per leg (use a chair or box for depth)
- 1.5‑rep squats or tempo squats (3s down, pause 1s, small up & full up): 3 × 8–10
- Single‑leg Romanian deadlift (slow): 4 × 6–8 each leg
- Broad jump or tuck jump (low impact, control): 3 × 6 — light plyometrics
- Side plank with leg raise: 3 × 15–20s per side

Weeks 7–8 (progressions)
- Increase sets/reps on compound movements. Try to perform at least 1–2 unassisted pull‑ups by end of week 8 if possible. Add tempo negatives and slow eccentrics on squats and single‑leg work. Introduce slow eccentric push‑ups (5s down) on two sets.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Strength & Skill (maximise bodyweight strength, target pull‑up and single‑arm/leg variations)
Goals: Achieve and increase sets of strict pull‑ups, harder pushing variations, pistols or near‑pistols, core strength and work capacity.

Weekly layout: 4 sessions (as before) with one optional conditioning day
- Day 1: Upper A (heavy)
- Day 2: Lower A (heavy)
- Day 3: Mobility/active recovery
- Day 4: Upper B (volume & skill)
- Day 5: Lower B + Core
- Days 6–7: Rest or light activity

Weeks 9–10
Upper A
- Warm‑up
- Strict pull‑ups: 5 sets × max reps (work to 3–6 each set). If >6 reps, increase difficulty (add slow negatives or chest‑to‑bar).
- Diamond or close‑hand push‑ups (adds triceps strength): 4 × 8–12

Cardio goals and how it fits the program
- Purpose: improve aerobic fitness, support recovery, aid conditioning and body composition without undermining strength gains.
- Priority order: keep strength sessions primary. Cardio should supplement, not replace, key strength work.
- Frequency: 2–4 cardio sessions/week depending on goals:
  - Strength/size focus: 2 sessions/week (low‑moderate intensity).
  - Recomposition or fat loss: 3–4 sessions/week (mix of steady and higher intensity).
  - Endurance focus: 3–4+ sessions, but expect slower strength progress if high volume.

How to place cardio around strength training
- Low‑intensity steady state (LISS): can be done same day as strength (after session) or on rest/active recovery days.
- High‑intensity interval training (HIIT): do on separate days from heavy lower‑body strength if possible, or after upper‑body sessions; avoid doing intense HIIT right before or after heavy leg sessions.
- Keep sessions 20–40 minutes. Longer sessions okay occasionally but increase recovery needs.

Space‑and‑noise‑friendly cardio options for a small flat
- Low impact cardio (minimal jumping/noise): marching/high‑knee march, low‑impact step touches, shadow boxing, incline walking on treadmill substitute (walking in place lifting knees), stationary cycling only if he has a bike.
- Higher intensity/noise: jumping jacks, squat jumps, burpees, mountain climbers, tuck jumps. Use sparingly if downstairs neighbours are an issue.
- Stair running (if building has stairs) — great for power and conditioning if available.
- Skipping rope: excellent if ceiling height and neighbours permit.
- Stair or step ups on a sturdy low step/chair (if safe).
- Tabata‑style circuits using bodyweight movements.

Cardio session types (with examples and progressions)
1) LISS (Low‑Intensity Steady State)
- Time: 25–45 minutes
- Examples: brisk walking (in place or around building), marching/high‑knee march with arm movement, shadow boxing at steady pace.
- Intensity: conversational pace, RPE 3–5/10; heart rate ~60–70% max.
- Benefits: recovery, fat oxidation, low interference with strength.
- Progression: increase duration +5–10 min or add light incline (longer stride or higher knee lift).

Sample LISS workout
- 30 min total: 5 min warm‑up march, 20 min steady march/high‑knee march, 5 min cooldown walk + mobility.

2) Moderate Interval Training (MIT) — short intervals, low impact
- Time: 20–30 minutes
- Format: 40s work / 20s rest × 10 rounds (total ~10 min work within 20 min session)
- Moves: alternating low‑impact movements — step touches, bodyweight squats, mountain climbers (slow), shadow boxing.
- Intensity: RPE 6–7/10.
- Progression: increase work interval to 45–50s, reduce rest, or add rounds.

3) HIIT — high intensity (sprints-style or bodyweight)
- Time: 10–20 minutes total
- Format examples:
  - Classic Tabata: 20s all‑out / 10s rest × 8 rounds = 4 min work + rest; repeat for 2–3 rounds with 2–3 min rest between.
  - EMOM sprint circuit: 10 rounds EMOM — minute 1: 30s burpees, rest remainder; minute 2: 30s mountain climbers – alternate.
- Moves: burpees, tuck jumps, squat jumps, high‑knees, skater hops. If noise is an issue substitute low‑impact options (fast mountain climbers from plank, quick step‑ups).
- Intensity: RPE 8–9/10.
- Progression: add rounds or increase interval duration, or shorten rest.

Sample HIIT session (noise‑conscious variant)
- 6 rounds of: 30s high‑knee march/high‑knee fast (no jump), 20s rest; 30s fast bodyweight squats (control, no jump), 40s rest between rounds. Total ~18 min.

4) Pyramid or Fartlek bodyweight cardio (fun and variable)
- Time: 20–30 minutes
- Example: 1 min easy, 1 min moderate, 1 min hard, 2 min easy, 2 min hard, 1 min moderate, 1 min easy — repeat sequence with movements like shadow boxing, fast step‑ups, burpees (or low‑impact equivalent).
- Good for variety, engagement, and mixing intensities.

5) Conditioning circuits that complement strength
- Short circuits mixing strength‑type bodyweight moves to build work capacity without heavy jumping.
- Example 3 rounds for time or EMOM:
  - 10 incline push‑ups
  - 8/leg reverse lunges (bodyweight)
  - 6 inverted rows (slow tempo)
  - 30s plank
  - Rest 60–90s between rounds
- Time: 20–30 minutes
- Use lighter loads/reps so strength quality isn’t lost.

Specific weekly examples to add to the 12‑week plan
A) Strength focus (2 cardio sessions/week)
- Tue (after Lower A strength or separate short walk): 25–30 min LISS walk or march.
- Sat/Sun: 20 min MIT (40s work/20s rest) — low impact.

B) Recomposition/fat loss (3 cardio sessions/week)
- Tue: 30–40 min LISS (walking/marching).
- Thu: 15–20 min HIIT (noise‑conscious: mountain climbers, squat pulses, shadow boxing).
- Sat: 25 min MIT/Conditioning circuit (moderate intensity).

C) Higher conditioning (4 sessions/week)
- Mon: 20 min LISS recovery (after Upper A)
- Wed: 15 min HIIT (short Tabata)
- Fri: 20 min MIT (intervals)
- Sun: 30–45 min long LISS (brisk walk or stair walking)

Progression framework
- Start conservative: first 1–2 weeks, keep cardio short and low intensity to avoid interfering with strength adaptation.
- Increase total weekly cardio volume by ~10% per week or add 1 session every 2–3 weeks depending on recovery.
- For HIIT: limit to 1–2 sessions/week to avoid recovery issues.
- Track RPE and resting HR if possible — rising resting HR or persistent fatigue indicates scale‑back.

Noise and neighbour considerations
- Prefer low‑impact variants (marching, step touches, shadow boxing).
- Use yoga mat and soft shoes; avoid repeated jumping near thin ceilings.
- Schedule HIIT sessions during daytime and ask clients to be mindful of neighbors.

Warm‑up and cooldown for cardio sessions
- Warm‑up: 3–5 min easy march, dynamic mobility (arm swings, leg swings).
- Cooldown: 3–5 min easy march/walk, stretching focusing on hips, calves, quads, and shoulders.

Monitoring and metrics
- Track session type, duration, perceived exertion (RPE), and heart rate if available.
- Aim for a weekly mix: 1–2 LISS, 1 MIT, and up to 1 HIIT as needed.
- Reassess aerobic fitness every 4 weeks by time to complete a fixed circuit or heart‑rate response — e.g., 12‑minute AMRAP (as many rounds as possible) of a set circuit, or a 2 km time‑trial on stairs/walking loop.

Sample integrated week (Strength + Cardio + Nutrition)
- Mon: Upper A strength + 10–15 min LISS cooldown (walk/march)
- Tue: Lower A strength; later 20–30 min LISS (or rest if fatigue)
- Wed: 20 min MIT (conditioning/light intervals) + mobility
- Thu: Upper B strength
- Fri: Lower B strength + optional 10–15 min easy walk
- Sat: HIIT 12–15 min (or long walk) OR rest depending on fatigue
- Sun: Rest + mobility

Final notes
- Keep cardio practical and enjoyable — shadow boxing, playlist intervals, or watching a show while marching can increase adherence.
- Emphasize the priority: do strength work first on days both occur. Cardio should not prevent completing the strength session at the intended intensity.
- If the client shows strength stagnation or excessive fatigue after adding cardio, scale back volume/intensity or shift some sessions to lower impact.

2) Flat or adjustable bench
- Why: For pressing, split squats with foot on bench, supported rows, step‑ups.

- Why: Easier deadlift pattern for beginners and back/leg development with less low‑back stress.

Great — here’s a fun, Saturday finisher day your client can do at home in the flat. It’s designed to be enjoyable, varied, and to build conditioning, core strength and work capacity without wrecking recovery for the main strength program. It’s optional but recommended most weeks. I give three themed formats to rotate week-to-week so it stays fresh, plus progressions, noise considerations, and recovery notes.

General structure (total time ~20–40 minutes)
- Warm‑up: 5–7 minutes dynamic — marching/jog in place, arm circles, leg swings, hip openers, 30s plank.
- Finisher: one of the themed workouts below (15–25 minutes).
- Cool‑down: 3–5 minutes easy mobility and breathing.

How to choose intensity
- Treat Saturday as an energetic, fun session — target RPE 6–8 depending on fatigue from the week.
- If he’s tired that week, choose the “Low‑impact Cardio + Core” or reduce rounds.
- Keep noise in mind — use low‑impact variants (marching, fast bodyweight squats rather than jumps) if neighbours are a concern.

Rotate these three themes each Saturday (A → B → C)

A) “Deck of Cards” Bodyweight Challenge — competitive and variable
- How it works: Assign each suit a bodyweight exercise. Shuffle a small deck (or use app/randomiser). Draw one card at a time; perform reps equal to the card value (J=11, Q=12, K=13, A=15) or use Ace=1/11 for flexibility. Continue for 10–15 cards or for 20 minutes.
- Suggested suit mapping (low‑noise-friendly):
  - Hearts: Incline push‑ups (hands on couch)
  - Diamonds: Bodyweight squats (fast but controlled)
  - Clubs: Australian rows / towel rows (under table) or band rows
  - Spades: Mountain climber pulses (low impact: slow steady pace) or slow plank shoulder taps for noise control
- Example rules: Draw 12 cards or set a 20-minute timer and draw until time’s up. Track total reps each week to compete with self next week.
- Progression: Increase to 15 cards or shorten rest between cards, use harder push variants or add weight vest when available.

B) “Circuit of Joy” — partnerless AMRAP (interval-based, can be music-driven)
- Format: 4 rounds AMRAP (as many rounds as possible) of 4 movements, each round 3–5 minutes, brief rest between rounds. Total ~20–25 min.
- Movements (example low‑impact, high fun):
  - 40s shadow boxing (fast arms, knees high optional)
  - 40s jump‑free burpee alternative (standing burpee: reach — no jump — squat to incline push‑up)
  - 40s kettlebell or dumbbell swing substitute (hip hinge with household weight or slow band RDL if no KB)
  - 40s plank to alternating toe touch (core)
  - 20–30s rest between rounds
- Score: Count full rounds + extra reps — keep a weekly leaderboard with himself.
- Progression: Increase each work interval to 50s, reduce rest, or change exercises to harder variants (real burpees, kettlebell swings).

C) “Skill & Play” — short skill practice + mini‑games (fun & low‑pressure)
- Format: 15–30 minutes focusing on a skill plus quick games.
- Components:
  1) Skill practice (8–12 min): Choose one skill — handstand prep (wall drills), pistol progressions (assisted), L‑sit progressions, or strict pull‑up practice. Do 6–8 short sets (10–30s work / rest equal time) focusing on quality.
  2) Mini‑games (8–15 min): Pick two of the following and do 3 rounds each:
     - “Beat the clock” — 60s: max incline push‑ups, rest 60s ×3
     - “Core bingo” — 30s each: hollow hold, side plank left, side plank right, dead bug; rotate with 30s rest.
     - “Quick ladder” — ladder 1–10 bodyweight squats and back down for speed (or 1–8 for time).
- Progression: Increase skill hold times, add more challenging skill variations, or make mini‑games longer/more rounds.

Noise‑sensitive substitutions
- Replace jumps with fast squats or step‑outs.
- Use standing burpee without the jump.
- For swings/jumps, substitute controlled kettlebell-like hip hinges or banded RDLs.

Scoring and motivation ideas
- Keep it fun: track simple metrics — total reps in Deck of Cards, rounds completed in Circuit, or hold times in Skill session.
- Small rewards: beat previous week’s score, or treat to a favorite healthy snack.
- Use music with a strong beat for circuits to increase enjoyment.

Below is a practical, repeatable mobility routine your client can do in the flat. It’s compact enough for daily use (10–20 minutes) and scalable for pre‑workout, post‑workout, or standalone recovery sessions. It targets the common tight/stiff areas that affect bodyweight strength work: shoulders/thoracic spine, hips, hamstrings, and ankles — plus core and wrist mobility for push/pull and handstand/pike work.

How to use it
- Pre‑workout (5–8 minutes): do the “Quick Activation” version to prime joints and movement patterns.
- Post‑workout (8–12 minutes): do the “Full Mobility” flow to restore range of motion and reduce soreness.
- Standalone recovery (15–20 minutes, 2–3×/week): do Full Mobility plus 2–3 minutes of breathing/relaxation.
- Tempo: move deliberately; avoid forcing range. Aim for pain‑free, mildly challenging stretches.
- Equipment: yoga mat, resistance band (optional), stool/chair for support.

Quick Activation (5–8 minutes) — ideal pre‑workout
1) Cat‑Cow with Thoracic Rotation — 1–2 minutes
- On hands and knees: 8–10 slow Cat/Cow cycles, then 5–6 controlled T‑spine rotations per side (thread‑the‑needle).
- Purpose: wake up thoracic mobility and spinal control.

2) World's Greatest Stretch (lunge + rotation) — 6–8 reps per side (dynamic)
- Step into a lunge, place opposite hand inside the front foot, rotate torso up toward ceiling reaching hand overhead, then return.
- Purpose: hip flexor/narrow hip opening + thoracic rotation.

3) Scapular Pulls + Scapular Push‑ups — 8–10 reps each
- Scapular pulls (hang or on bar): shrug shoulders up a little then depress; or from standing, door frame scapular retraction/protraction.
- Scapular push‑ups: from plank, squeeze shoulder blades together then push apart.
- Purpose: prime scapular control for pull‑ups and push‑ups.

4) Hip Hinge Drill (glute bridge → single‑leg RDL reach) — 8–10 reps
- Glute bridge x5 slow, then 6 slow single‑leg RDL reaches per side (bodyweight).
- Purpose: activate posterior chain.

5) Ankle mobility march (knee‑over‑toe step in place) — 30–60s
- March focusing on ankle dorsiflexion and controlled foot placement.

Full Mobility Flow (8–12 minutes) — best post‑workout or standalone
Start with 1 minute easy breathing or foam rolling (if available). Move through each exercise with controlled tempo. Hold static stretches 30–60s where indicated; do dynamic moves for 6–10 reps.

1) Thoracic spine & shoulders
- Thoracic extension over rolled towel or small pillow (or on a chair back) — 2 × 30s
- Wall angels or standing banded shoulder dislocations (use band or towel) — 2 × 8–10
- Pec doorway stretch (one arm at a time) — 2 × 30s per side

2) Lat & upper back release (band or doorway)
- Banded lat stretch (anchor band overhead and lean away) or kneeling lat stretch reaching overhead — 2 × 30s per side

3) Hip mobility sequence
- Couch/half‑kneeling quad/hip flexor stretch — 2 × 30s per side
- 90/90 hip switch (internal/external rotation) — 2 × 8 per side (slow, controlled)
- Deep squat hold (assisted with hold on door or chair if needed) — 2 × 30s
- World's Greatest Stretch (slow dynamic) — 6 reps each side

4) Hamstring & calf mobility
- Seated single‑leg hamstring reach (or standing hamstring windmills) — 2 × 30s per leg
- Calf wall stretch (knee straight & bent) — 2 × 30s per side

5) Ankle & foot mobility
- Kneeling ankle rock (shin vertical ankle dorsiflexion) — 2 × 10 each side
- Toe spread and foot doming (plantar intrinsic activation) — 2 × 10

6) Wrist & forearm mobility (for push/pull work)
- Wrist flexor and extensor stretches — 2 × 20–30s each direction per hand
- Tabletop wrist circles and gentle loaded wrist flexion (on hands) — 2 × 8–10

7) Core/doorway hang & decompress (if bar available)
- Dead hang or scapular hang on pull‑up bar: 3 × 10–20s (work to longer as tolerated)
- Supine knee hugs into chest with breathing: 2 × 30s to finish

Mobility Mini‑Routines (pick one if short on time)
- Upper body focus (5 min): Cat‑Cow + T‑spine rotations 1 min, Wall angels 1 min, Door pec stretch 1 min each side.
- Lower body focus (5 min): World's Greatest Stretch 1 min each side, Deep squat hold 1 min, Hamstring reach 1 min each leg.
- Wrists & shoulders (4 min): Wrist circles/stretches 1.5 min, Scapular pulls/push‑ups 1.5 min, Pec stretch 30s each.

Progressions and regressions
- If very stiff: increase time in holds, do mobility every day, and add soft tissue work. Use a band to assist stretches (e.g., banded shoulder dislocations).
- If too intense: reduce hold times to 15–20s, perform dynamic versions rather than holds.
- For improving thoracic extension, add 1–2 min daily of foam rolling or towel thoracic extension (over a rolled towel).

Weekly placement suggestions
- Pre‑strength session: Quick Activation (5–8 min) each training day.
- Post‑strength session: 6–10 min of Full Mobility focusing on the area worked (shoulders after upper days; hips/ankles after lower days).
- Saturday finisher day: add a 5–8 minute mobility cooldown from the Full Flow.
- Rest days: do a 10–15 minute Full Mobility session (choose areas that feel tight).

Tracking and outcomes
- Encourage him to notice movement quality improvements (deeper squat, better push‑up mechanics, easier overhead positions).
- Reassess mobility every 2–3 weeks: can he get deeper into squat? reach overhead with arms straight? hang comfortably from bar for longer?
- If persistent limitations remain (e.g., shoulder pain, severe ankle restriction), advise a professional assessment.

- Hip prep: World’s Greatest Stretch 6 each side

- Ankles: Kneeling ankle rock 10 each side
- Wrists: Wrist flexor/extensor stretch 30s per side

- Finish: 2 min deep breathing

- Warm‑up: ~5–8 minutes before every session (Quick Activation from Mobility: Cat‑Cow/T‑spine threads, World's Greatest stretch, scapular pulls, hip hinge drill, ankle march).
- Cool‑down/mobility: 6–12 minutes after sessions (Full Mobility flow focusing on area trained).
- Progression principles: aim for progressive overload by reducing assistance, increasing difficulty (body angle/leverage), adding reps/sets, increasing tempo control (slow eccentrics), or adding weight (vest/dumbbells/bands) when available.
- Phase 2 push intensity uses strength‑focused approach: heavier/advanced push variants, lower reps (3–6) and longer rests (2–3 min).
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions/week built in (mix of LISS, MIT, 1 HIIT per week max). Keep strength priority; avoid hard HIIT on heavy lower‑body days.
- Mobility: Quick Activation pre‑workout; Full Mobility post‑workout or on recovery days.
- Nutrition: Use earlier guidance. If you give his weight I’ll calculate exact calories; otherwise start with maintenance = bodyweight (kg) ×30 kcal and adjust (+250 kcal for gain). Protein ~2.0 g/kg. Creatine 5 g/day optional.
- Equipment suggestions: bands, pull‑up bar (already have), weight vest, adjustable dumbbells/kettlebell later for progression. Program notes where to use bands/vest/dumbbells.

Progression cadence
- Each 4‑week block: 3 progressive weeks + 1 lighter “deload/technique” week (week 4, 8, 12 are lighter/tech focus / test weeks).
- Weekly targets: increase reps or reduce assistance for main movements each progressive week. On deload week reduce total sets by ~25% or use easier variants but keep 1–2 high quality sets for skill.

Notation
- RPE guidance approximate: 1–10 scale.
- Tempo: e.g., 3–1–1 means 3s eccentric, 1s pause bottom, 1s concentric.
- If client can’t do full movement, use regressions listed.

PHASE 1 — Weeks 1–4: FOUNDATIONS (motor control, baseline strength, joint durability)
Goals: build movement quality, core stability, scapular control, begin pull/push patterns and single‑leg work.

Weekly schedule (repeat weeks 1–3 progressive; week 4 lighter)
- Mon: Upper A (push focus)
- Tue: Lower A (single‑leg focus)
- Wed: Cardio LISS + Mobility (active recovery)
- Thu: Upper B (pull focus)
- Fri: Lower B + Core
- Sat: Finisher (rotate A/B/C)
- Sun: Rest / Full Mobility session (optional)

Weeks 1–3 — Progress by 1–2 reps per set or add 1 set per main movement each week; reduce assistance on pulls gradually.

Week 1 (example session templates)
Upper A
- Warm‑up: Quick Activation 6–8 min
- Incline push‑ups (hands on couch) 4 × 8–10 (RPE 6–7) tempo 2–0–1 rest 60–90s
- Scapular pull‑ups / scapular retractions on bar or door frame 3 × 8–10 (focus on shrugs and depressions) rest 60s
- Towel/inverted rows under table 4 × 8–10 rest 60–90s
- Pike press (wall pike) 3 × 6–8 rest 60–90s
- Plank 3 × 30s (technique) rest 45–60s
- Cool‑down: 6 min Full Mobility (upper emphasis: thoracic, pec stretch, lats)

Lower A
- Warm‑up
- Split squat (rear foot supported or stationary) 3 × 8–10/leg tempo 3–0–1 rest 60–90s
- Glute bridge 3 × 12–15 rest 45–60s
- Single‑leg RDL (BW) 3 × 8/leg rest 60–90s
- Calf raises 3 × 15 rest 30–45s
- Dead bug 3 × 8–10/side
- Cool‑down: hip flexor, deep squat hold, hamstring mobility

Wed — Cardio (LISS)
- 30 min brisk walk in place / march or external walk; low impact RPE 3–4
- Mobility: 8–10 min Full Mobility (lower focus)

Upper B
- Warm‑up
- Assisted pull‑ups / eccentrics 4 × 3–5 slow negative (4–5s) rest 90–120s
- Incline push‑ups or knee push‑ups 4 × 10–12 rest 60–90s
- Australian rows or towel rows 4 × 8–12 rest 60–90s
- Side plank 2 × 20s/side
- Hollow body hold 3 × 20s
- Cool‑down: thoracic + shoulder mobility

Lower B + Core
- Warm‑up
- Air squats 4 × 12–15 tempo 3s down, pause 1s rest 60–90s
- Reverse lunges 3 × 8–10/leg rest 60–90s
- Hip thrust (single/double) 3 × 10–12 rest 60–90s
- Bird‑dog 3 × 8/side
- Hanging knee raises or lying leg raises 3 × 8–12
- Cool‑down: calves/hamstrings/hips

Sat — Finisher (Week 1 choose A: Deck of Cards)
- Warm‑up 5 min
- Deck of Cards (10 cards or 15 min timer) suit mapping:
  Hearts = incline push‑ups
  Diamonds = bodyweight squats (controlled)
  Clubs = towel rows (or band rows)
  Spades = plank shoulder taps (low weight on ceiling)
- Cool‑down 4–6 min mobility

Week 2 — increase reps or add 1 set to main lifts; reduce assistance slightly on pulls (shorter negative time to 4s → 3s if capable).

Week 3 — continue progression: aim for fewer assisted negatives and longer sets on rows; add 1–2s eccentrics on push‑ups for control.

Week 4 — Deload / technique week
- Reduce volume ~25%: do 3 sets on main lifts, keep reps moderate, focus on slow eccentrics and perfect technique.
- Use upper/lower sessions but reduce accessory volume.
- Saturday: Skill & Play finisher (low volume focusing on handstand/pull practice).

PHASE 2 — Weeks 5–8: BUILD (increased intensity; push days strength-focused)
Goals: increase maximal pressing strength with low‑rep, higher difficulty push progressions; increase single‑leg strength and time under tension; accumulate pull volume toward unassisted pull‑ups.

Weekly schedule (repeat weekly; week 8 is lighter/test)
- Mon: Upper A (Push — HIGH INTENSITY strength focus)
- Tue: Lower A (single‑leg + explosiveness)
- Wed: Cardio MIT + Mobility (active)
- Thu: Upper B (Pull + secondary push)
- Fri: Lower B + Core + optional short LISS
- Sat: Finisher (rotate B or C)
- Sun: Rest / Full Mobility

Phase 2 push intensity approach: Strength‑focused (Option 2). Main pushes use harder progressions (elevated/weighted/archer) at 3–6 reps, 4–6 sets, 2–3 min rest. Secondary push/horizontal work 3–4 sets × 6–8. Use bands/vest/dumbbells if available.

Weeks 5–7 — progressive increase in difficulty each week; Week 8 — lighter/test week (reduce volume, test pull‑up max).

Week 5 (example)
Upper A (Push heavy)
- Warm‑up: Quick Activation 6–8 min
- Main heavy push — Elevated or Weighted Push‑ups (feet elevated on couch or wear 5–10 kg vest if available): 5 × 4–6 reps tempo 2–0–1 rest 2.5–3 min. If no elevation/vest, do archer push‑ups 4–6 reps/side.
- Secondary horizontal push — Archer push‑ups / staggered hands: 4 × 6–8/side rest 90–120s
- Vertical press — Pike push‑ups (elevate feet to increase angle) 4 × 6–8 rest 90–120s
- Accessory triceps band pressdowns / close‑grip push‑ups 3 × 10–12 rest 60–90s
- Core — L‑sit progression (tuck L‑sit on floor or between chairs) 3 × 10–20s
- Cool‑down: shoulder/thoracic mobility 8–10 min

Lower A
- Warm‑up
- Box‑supported pistol progressions / assisted pistol 4 × 5–8/leg rest 90–120s
- 1.5‑rep tempo squats 3 × 8–10 tempo 3s down, pause, small up, full up rest 90s
- Single‑leg RDL (slow) 4 × 6–8/leg rest 90s
- Low‑impact plyo (controlled broad jump or tuck jump substitute) 3 × 6 — optional
- Side plank + leg raise 3 × 15–20s/side
- Cool‑down: hips/ankles

Wed — Cardio MIT (40s work / 20s rest × 10 rounds = ~20 min total)
- Choose low‑impact moves: step touches, banded RDLs, shadow boxing, slow mountain climbers
- Mobility: 8–10 min (lower focus)

Upper B (Pull emphasis)
- Warm‑up
- Pull‑up practice: assisted pull‑ups / banded or foot‑assisted 5 × 3–6 (work to reduce assistance) rest 2–3 min
- Inverted rows (feet elevated) 4 × 8–12 rest 90s
- Incline push‑ups (for horizontal volume, lighter than Mon) 3 × 10–12
- Banded face pulls or banded rear delt work 3 × 12–15
- Core: hollow rocks 3 × 10–20
- Cool‑down: upper mobility

Lower B + Core
- Warm‑up
- Bulgarian split squats (full depth) 4 × 8/leg rest 90s
- Nordic curl progression substitute (towel slide hamstring curls) 3 × 6–8 eccentrics slow
- Hip thrust (single/double) 3 × 10–12
- Single‑leg calf raise 4 × 10–15
- Hanging knee raises 3 × 10–12
- Optional short easy LISS 10–15 min if recovered
- Cool‑down mobility

Sat — Finisher Circuit of Joy (choose B)
- Warm‑up 5
- 4 rounds AMRAP each round 3.5 min work / 30s rest: Shadow boxing 40s, standing burpee (no jump) + incline push‑ups 40s, band RDL 40s, plank toe taps 40s.
- Cool‑down 5 min

Week 6 — progressions
- Increase difficulty on main push by lowering reps in range but making movement harder (less assistance, higher feet, heavier vest). Keep sets. Slightly increase single‑leg difficulty (lower box height for pistols). Increase pull volume (add one extra set of rows or negatives).

Week 7 — continued progression
- Aim that by end of Week 7 client can perform at least 1–2 unassisted pull‑ups or improved eccentric control. Increase intensity on elevated push sets (use tempo negatives on 1–2 sets).

Week 8 — Test/Deload
- Reduce total volume ~25% across sessions; keep intensity on 1–2 heavy sets for technique.
- Test day (choose a day with full recovery—Thursday recommended) to assess:
  - Max strict pull‑ups for sets (record best single set)
  - Max push‑ups in good form (1‑min test or 3 sets to near failure)
  - Pistol progression level
- Saturday finisher: Skill & Play (lower intensity, work on pull/push skill, handstand prep)

PHASE 3 — Weeks 9–12: STRENGTH & SKILL (peak bodyweight strength)
Goals: consolidate gains, increase pull‑up sets & push strength, achieve pistols or near‑pistols, advanced core work. Week 12 is lighter/test week and wrap.

Weekly schedule
- Mon: Upper A (heavy pull focus + heavy push main)
- Tue: Lower A (heavy single‑leg and hamstring emphasis)
- Wed: Active recovery or Cardio HIIT (short/noise sensitive) + mobility
- Thu: Upper B (volume & skill)
- Fri: Lower B + Core (power & conditioning)
- Sat: Finisher (rotate fun A/B/C)
- Sun: Rest / Full Mobility

Weeks 9–10 — heavy work and skill accumulation
Week 9 (example)
Upper A
- Warm‑up
- Strict pull‑ups: 5 sets × max reps (aim 3–6 each; if >6 progress difficulty with slow negatives or weighted vest if available). Rest 2–3 min.
- Diamond/close hand push‑ups (weighted or elevated if needed) 4 × 8–12 rest 90–120s
- Archer/assisted one‑arm push‑up progressions 3 × 4–6/side rest 90–120s
- Inverted rows (feet elevated, slow tempo) 4 × 8–12 rest 90s
- L‑sit progressions (tuck L‑sit -> single‑leg L‑sit) 3 × 15–30s
- Cool‑down mobility

Lower A
- Warm‑up
- Pistol squats to full or box (attempt full) 4 × 4–6/leg rest 90–120s
- Shrimp squat progressions 3 × 6/leg rest 90s
- Single‑leg RDL slow 4 × 6–8/leg
- Nordic hamstring curl substitute (slow eccentrics, controlled slide) 3 × 6–8
- Calf work single‑leg 4 × 10–15
- Cool‑down mobility

Wed — Cardio HIIT (short, noise-conscious)
- 12–15 min total: Tabata style 20s on/10s off × 8 rounds of low noise moves (fast mountain climbers, standing burpee no jump, shadow boxing). Repeat for 2 rounds with 2–3 min rest between. Mobility after.

Upper B (volume & skill)
- Warm‑up
- Pull‑up ladder: 6–8 sets of 2–5 reps (short rest) to accumulate volume without maxing. Rest 60–90s between sets. Focus on form.
- Handstand prep / pike press advanced sets 6 × 20–40s of wall holds/handstand practice or 4 × 6 pike presses.
- Incline or paused push‑ups 4 × 8–10 (2s pause at bottom)
- Banded face pulls 3 × 12–15
- Core: hanging leg raises to toes progression 4 × 6–10
- Cool‑down mobility

Lower B + Core
- Warm‑up
- Bulgarian split squats heavy 4 × 6–8/leg rest 90–120s
- Slow single‑leg RDL / tempo 4 × 6/leg
- Hip thrust heavy single/double 4 × 8–10
- Conditioning: 6–8 rounds of 20s work/40s rest — step ups or fast bodyweight squats (low noise) — optional
- Core circuit: 3 rounds — 15 hollow rocks, 10 Russian twists (no twist if back pain), 30s plank
- Cool‑down mobility

Weeks 11–12 — peak & consolidation
Week 11 — push/pull intensity maintained; increase pull weekly volume (add another ladder or extra set). Aim for consistent multiple pull‑ups across sets.

Week 12 — Final test/deload
- Reduce volume ~25% but include 1 heavy day for testing:
  - Pull‑up test: 3 sets max with good rest; record best set.
  - Push‑up test: best 1‑minute or 3 sets to near failure.
  - Pistol attempt/progression test.
- Saturday finisher: favorite rotated finisher at moderate intensity.
- Conclude with a 15–20 minute Full Mobility session and plan next steps (add equipment, shift to dumbbell/barbell program).

Safety, tracking and cues
- Emphasize form over reps. If pain (sharp or joint), regress and assess.
- Track these weekly metrics: pull‑up max, push‑up max (or 1‑min), RPE on main sets, bodyweight (if monitoring composition), sleep and energy.
- Encourage 7–9 hours sleep/night and protein at each meal.
